options.label: Activate air filtration
options.tooltip: Activate for better air filtration. G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

options.label: During print
options.tooltip: Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code during print.

options.label: On completion
options.tooltip: Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code after print completion.

options.label: Activate temperature control
options.tooltip:
Enable this option for automated chamber temperature control. This option activates the emitting of an M191 command before the "machine_start_gcode"
 which sets the chamber temperature and waits until it is reached. In addition, it emits an M141 command at the end of the print to turn off the chamber heater, if present.

This option relies on the firmware supporting the M191 and M141 commands either via macros or natively and is usually used when an active chamber heater is installed.

options.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance (beta)
options.tooltip:
With increasing print speeds (and hence increasing volumetric flow through the nozzle) and increasing accelerations, it has been observed that the effective PA value typically decreases. This means that a single PA value is not always 100% optimal for all features and a compromise value is usually used that does not cause too much bulging on features with lower flow speed and accelerations while also not causing gaps on faster features.

This feature aims to address this limitation by modeling the response of your printer's extrusion system depending on the volumetric flow speed and acceleration it is printing at. Internally, it generates a fitted model that can extrapolate the needed pressure advance for any given volumetric flow speed and acceleration, which is then emitted to the printer depending on the current print conditions.

When enabled, the pressure advance value above is overridden. However, a reasonable default value above is strongly recommended to act as a fallback and for when tool changing.

options.label: Pressure advance for bridges
options.tooltip:
Pressure advance value for bridges. Set to 0 to disable.

A lower PA value when printing bridges helps reduce the appearance of slight under extrusion immediately after bridges. This is caused by the pressure drop in the nozzle when printing in the air and a lower PA helps counteract this.

options.label: Adaptive pressure advance measurements (beta)
options.tooltip:
Add sets of pressure advance (PA) values, the volumetric flow speeds and accelerations they were measured at, separated by a comma. One set of values per line. For example
0.04,3.96,3000
0.033,3.96,10000
0.029,7.91,3000
0.026,7.91,10000

How to calibrate:
1. Run the pressure advance test for at least 3 speeds per acceleration value. It is recommended that the test is run for at least the speed of the external perimeters, the speed of the internal perimeters and the fastest feature print speed in your profile (usually its the sparse or solid infill). Then run them for the same speeds for the slowest and fastest print accelerations, and no faster than the recommended maximum acceleration as given by the Klipper input shaper
2. Take note of the optimal PA value for each volumetric flow speed and acceleration. You can find the flow number by selecting flow from the color scheme drop down and move the horizontal slider over the PA pattern lines. The number should be visible at the bottom of the page. The ideal PA value should be decreasing the higher the volumetric flow is. If it is not, confirm that your extruder is functioning correctly. The slower and with less acceleration you print, the larger the range of acceptable PA values. If no difference is visible, use the PA value from the faster test
3. Enter the triplets of PA values, Flow and Accelerations in the text box here and save your filament profile.

options.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance for overhangs (beta)
options.tooltip: Enable adaptive PA for overhangs as well as when flow changes within the same feature. This is an experimental option, as if the PA profile is not set accurately, it will cause uniformity issues on the external surfaces before and after overhangs.

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip:
Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)

options.label: Full fan speed at layer
options.tooltip:
Auxiliary fan speed will be ramped up linearly from layer "For the first" to maximum at layer "Full fan speed at layer".
"Full fan speed at layer" will be ignored if lower than "For the first", in which case the fan will run at maximum allowed speed at layer "For the first" + 1.

options.label: Chamber minimal temperature
options.tooltip:
This is the chamber temperature at which printing should start, while the chamber continues heating toward the "Target" chamber temperature. For example, set the Target to 60 and the Minimal to 50 to begin printing once the chamber reaches 50°C, without waiting for the full 60°C.

It sets a G-code variable named chamber_minimal_temperature, which can be passed to your print start macro or a heat soak macro, like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_MIN_TEMP=[chamber_minimal_temperature].

Unlike the "Target" chamber temperature, this option does not emit any M141/M191 commands; it only exposes the value to your custom G-code. It should not exceed the "Target" chamber temperature.

options.label: Chamber temperature
options.tooltip:
For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air filtration for ABS and ASA.

For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled (set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by material softening at the heat break.

If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]. This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed.

options.label: For the first
options.tooltip: Set special auxiliary cooling fan for the first certain layers.

options.label: No cooling for the first
options.tooltip: Turn off all cooling fans for the first few layers. This can be used to improve build plate adhesion.

options.label: Condition
options.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

options.label: Condition
options.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan after printing completes.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

options.label: Default color
options.tooltip:
Default filament color.
Right click to reset value to system default.

options.label: Don't slow down outer walls
options.tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan during printing. This speed will override the speed in filament custom G-code.

options.label: Force cooling for overhangs and bridges
options.tooltip: Enable this option to allow adjustment of the part cooling fan speed for specifically for overhangs, internal and external bridges. Setting the fan speed specifically for these features can improve overall print quality and reduce warping.

options.label: Enable pressure advance
options.tooltip: Enable pressure advance, auto calibration result will be overwritten once enabled.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

options.label: Layer time
options.tooltip: Part cooling fan will be enabled for layers of which estimated time is shorter than this value. Fan speed is interpolated between the minimum and maximum fan speeds according to layer printing time.

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip: Part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

options.label: Adaptive volumetric speed
options.tooltip:
When enabled, the extrusion flow is limited by the smaller of the fitted value (calculated from line width and layer height) and the user-defined maximum flow. When disabled, only the user-defined maximum flow is applied.

Note: Experimental and incomplete feature imported from BBS. Functional for some profiles that already have the variable saved.

options.label: Adhesiveness Category
options.tooltip: Filament category.

options.label: Change extrusion role G-code (filament)
options.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed for the active filament.

options.label: Filament ramming length
options.tooltip: When changing the extruder, it is recommended to extrude a certain length of filament from the original extruder. This helps minimize nozzle oozing.

options.label: Wipe tower cooling
options.tooltip: Temperature drop before entering filament tower

options.label: Speed of the last cooling move
options.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

options.label: Speed of the first cooling move
options.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

options.label: Number of cooling moves
options.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

options.label: Price
options.tooltip: Filament price. For statistics only.

options.label: Density
options.tooltip: Filament density. For statistics only.

options.label: De-retraction Speed
options.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

options.label: Diameter
options.tooltip: Filament diameter is used to calculate extrusion in G-code, so it is important and should be accurate.

options.label: End G-code
options.tooltip: End G-code when finishing the printing of this filament.

options.label: Filament's extruder variant
options.tooltip: Filament's extruder variant.

options.label: Flow ratio
options.tooltip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

options.label: Flush temperature
options.tooltip: Temperature when flushing filament. 0 indicates the upper bound of the recommended nozzle temperature range.

options.label: Flush volumetric speed
options.tooltip: Volumetric speed when flushing filament. 0 indicates the max volumetric speed.

options.label: Ironing flow
options.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing flow. This allows you to customize the ironing flow for each filament type. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

options.label: Ironing inset
options.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing inset. This allows you to customize the distance to keep from the edges when ironing for each filament type.

options.label: Ironing line spacing
options.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing line spacing. This allows you to customize the spacing between ironing lines for each filament type.

options.label: Ironing speed
options.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing speed. This allows you to customize the print speed of ironing lines for each filament type.

options.label: Support material
options.tooltip: Support material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

options.label: Loading speed
options.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

options.label: Loading speed at the start
options.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

options.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

options.label: Max volumetric speed
options.tooltip: This setting stands for how much volume of filament can be melted and extruded per second. Printing speed is limited by max volumetric speed, in case of too high and unreasonable speed setting. Can't be zero.

options.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
options.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Orca Slicer will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

options.label: Enable ramming for multi-tool setups
options.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multi-tool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the tool change. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

options.label: Multi-tool ramming flow
options.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the tool change.

options.label: Multi-tool ramming volume
options.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the tool change.

options.label: Filament notes
options.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

options.label: Filament printable
options.tooltip: The filament is printable in extruder.

options.label: Ramming parameters
options.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

options.label: Retract amount before wipe
options.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

options.label: Only lift Z above
options.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

options.label: Only lift Z below
options.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

options.label: On surfaces
options.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

options.label: Extra length on restart
options.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

options.label: Retract when change layer
options.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

options.label: Retraction distance when cut
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

options.label: Retraction Length
options.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

options.label: Travel distance threshold
options.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

options.label: Retraction Speed
options.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

options.label: Shrinkage (XY)
options.tooltip:
Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in XY to compensate. For multi-material prints, ensure filament shrinkage matches across all used filaments
Be sure to allow enough space between objects, as this compensation is done after the checks.

options.label: Shrinkage (Z)
options.tooltip: Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in Z to compensate.

options.label: Soluble material
options.tooltip: Soluble material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

options.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
options.tooltip: If set to non-zero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

options.label: Stamping loading speed
options.tooltip: Speed used for stamping.

options.label: Start G-code
options.tooltip: Start G-code when starting the printing of this filament.

options.label: Delay after unloading
options.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable tool changes with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

options.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion distance
options.tooltip: Pre-extrusion distance for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

options.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion length
options.tooltip: Pre-extrusion length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

options.label: Interface layer print temperature
options.tooltip: Print temperature for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet). If set to -1, use max recommended nozzle temperature.

options.label: Interface layer purge length
options.tooltip: Purge length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

options.label: Tower ironing area
options.tooltip: Ironing area for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

options.label: Type
options.tooltip: The material type of filament.

options.label: Unloading speed
options.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect initial part of unloading just after ramming).

options.label: Unloading speed at the start
options.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

options.label: Vendor
options.tooltip: Vendor of filament. For show only.

options.label: Wipe while retracting
options.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

options.label: Wipe Distance
options.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

options.label: Z-hop height
options.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

options.label: Z-hop type
options.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

options.label: Fan speed
options.tooltip: Special auxiliary cooling fan speed, effective only for the first x layers.

options.label: Full fan speed at layer
options.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

options.label: Idle temperature
options.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups. This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Inherits profile
options.tooltip: Name of parent profile.

options.label: Internal bridges fan speed
options.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

options.label: Ironing fan speed
options.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

options.label: Nozzle temperature
options.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for layers after the initial one.

options.label: First layer nozzle temperature
options.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for printing the first layer when using this filament.

options.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
options.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

options.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
options.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

options.label: Pellet flow coefficient
options.tooltip:
Pellet flow coefficient is empirically derived and allows for volume calculation for pellet printers.

Internally it is converted to filament_diameter. All other volume calculations remain the same.

filament_diameter = sqrt( (4 * pellet_flow_coefficient) / PI )

options.label: Pressure advance
options.tooltip: Pressure advance (Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor (Marlin).

options.label: Keep fan always on
options.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that the part cooling fan will never stop completely and will run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

options.label: Required nozzle HRC
options.tooltip: Minimum HRC of nozzle required to print the filament. Zero means no checking of nozzle's HRC.

options.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
options.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to make the final layer time not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that layer can be cooled for longer time. This can improve the cooling quality for needle and small details.

options.label: Layer time
options.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

options.label: Min print speed
options.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

options.label: Support interface fan speed
options.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

options.label: Softening temperature
options.tooltip: The material softens at this temperature, so when the bed temperature is equal to or greater than this, it's highly recommended to open the front door and/or remove the upper glass to avoid clogging.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

options.label: Bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature for layers except the initial one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.

options.label: First layer bed temperature
options.tooltip: Bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.
